The map

Left to right is dependency — each phase is unusable without the one before it. P0 is what you are interviewed on, P1 is the substrate it stands on. Phase 0 carries no AI on purpose; that is what fixes the actual gap.

Every line has a destination

This is the fix for staring at a topic with nowhere to go. All 1306 work items carry a link; the 18 that don't are the five ship-and-apply days whose source line literally reads “no new material” — those are marked own work.

ChipWhat it isCount
▶ 4:34:10 A verified deep link. Someone read the transcript at that timestamp and recorded the sentence they heard — hover the chip to see it. This is the strongest destination on the page.63
⌥ servers/src/filesystem/index.ts Working code — the exact file, not the repo. On every one of the 500 build tasks. Solid border means it points at a single file or a doc anchor whose runnable snippet is right there; dashed means the example project for that topic area, where you may still need to look around. File paths come from the repositories' real git trees, and all 65 locations are verified. Not a solution to your exact task — those are yours to write, and no published one exists — but the specific file doing the same thing.500
⚙ Node — HTTP module The reference for that specific task, matched on the API the task actually names — http, pgvector, checkpoint, OpenTelemetry. Official docs, all 64 verified to resolve. Not a worked solution: your build is yours, this is the page that tells you how the thing works.230
▶ named video The link that line already carried in the curriculum — its own short video or doc.100
▶ build-along The unit's video, for a task that names no specific API. A video at least shows the work being done.349
⧉ unit source Last resort: the unit's source, telling you which video or doc the line comes from, not where inside it.546
own work No external source by design — a ship, polish or application day.18

Each unit also lists every source it has, and for the 44 units whose video publishes a chapter list, all its chapters as individual deep links — real scraped data, so you can jump to the right part yourself. No timestamp on this page is guessed. Two automated chapter-to-topic matchers were tried during this repo's history and both produced confident, mostly wrong results, so where a verified timestamp doesn't exist you get the source and the chapter list instead of a fabricated one.

How the minutes work

Each day is exactly 240 minutes — that is the hard cap, and no day on this page exceeds it. Each unit's section budgets are the ones the curriculum itself states (Intake 2.5h, Build 2.5h, Consolidate 1h, or Study/Produce/Practise in the final phase), split across that section's lines and rounded to five minutes. Because a 6-hour unit does not fit in a 4-hour day, work carries over: a line marked 1/2 continues tomorrow. 140 lines split this way. Only 4 lines are set by a real runtime rather than the split — those are amber. Treat every number as a ceiling, not a target.

Combining AI with the map

Every foundation topic is taught beside the LLM problem it becomes, so agents in Phase 2 land on ground you have already walked. Twelve of the ninety-one pairings:

The unit's own topicIts LLM counterpart, same day
U1 The Node runtime and the event loopStream a model's response through the hand-rolled http server you just wrote — no framework, no SDK, just res.write() per chunk.
U3 REST design and runtime validationExpose your notes CRUD as a tool schema for a model — the same Zod objects, converted with z.toJSONSchema. One schema, two consumers.
U7 SQL you can write without an ORMHave a model write three of today's queries from your schema alone, then run EXPLAIN on each and grade them against the ones you wrote by hand.
U10 Migrations as a disciplineWrite the migration that adds CREATE EXTENSION vector and an embedding vector(1536) column to a table that already has rows.
U13 TypeScript beyond the basicsType a tool registry so that each tool's handler receives exactly its own inferred argument type — generics plus a mapped type, no any anywhere.
U23 Cost, caching, and model routingRoute by task, not by vibe: cheap model for classification and extraction, expensive model for synthesis. Measure the quality drop on each before you keep it.
U29 Measuring retrievalHand-label 30 query/document pairs. This is the unglamorous hour that makes every later claim about retrieval quality real.
U34 Tracing and observabilityTrace one request end to end: retrieval, rerank, prompt assembly, model call, parse. Every span carries tokens, cost and latency.
U39 Security: injection, rate limits, abuseAttack your own retrieval: put ignore previous instructions inside a document you ingest, then ask a question that retrieves it.
U48 Termination, budgets, and safety railsGive the loop three independent stops: max iterations, max tokens, max wall-clock. Trip each one on purpose and confirm it halts cleanly.
U69 Database at scaleLoad a million rows into your Day 31 table and re-measure. HNSW build time and index memory are the two numbers that decide whether Postgres stays your vector store.
U78 Service decompositionSplit on the seam that actually exists in an LLM product: ingestion, retrieval, inference and orchestration scale on different axes and fail differently.

The four hard gates

Nothing ships → repeat the week.

Phase endsDayDatePasses when
Foundation repairDay 27Wed, 30 Sept 2026 a stranger can clone, follow the README, and have it running — and the live URL works.
AI engineering coreDay 63Wed, 11 Nov 2026 live URL works, eval report is public, traces flow in production.
Agents & MCPDay 99Wed, 23 Dec 2026 live URL, public eval report, traces flowing, and someone else completed a task with it.
Production & scaleDay 126Sat, 23 Jan 2027 all three projects are live, documented, reproducible, and evidenced.
